topic: The Fractal Path: Ternary Logic and the Constrained Towers of Hanoi
target_audience: University students (Computer Science/Mathematics) or advanced high school students

sections.title: Introduction: The Restricted Puzzle
lecture_lines: Here is the classic Towers of Hanoi puzzle setup.
Direct jumps between Peg A and C are forbidden.
Disks can only move between adjacent neighboring pegs.
Every shift must pass through the middle peg, B.
Our goal is moving all disks from A to C.
animations: FadeIn three vertical pegs labeled A, B, and C (#FFFFFF) and 3 disks on Peg A (#FF5733, #33FF57, #3357FF).
Draw a red cross (#FF0000) over a dashed curved arrow between Peg A and Peg C.
Display green double-headed arrows (#00FF00) between Pegs A-B and Pegs B-C.
Animate the smallest disk (#3357FF) sliding from Peg A to Peg B, then from Peg B to Peg C.
Flash the three disks on Peg C and highlight the start (A) and end (C) pegs.

sections.title: Prerequisite: Base-3 (Ternary) Counting
lecture_lines: Ternary counting uses digits zero, one, and two.
Watch the counter increment in base-three logic.
Each digit maps to a specific peg: A, B, or C.
animations: Display a 3-digit ternary counter '000' where each digit represents a disk [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/disk.svg] position.
Animate the counter incrementing through 000, 001, 002, 010 (Base-3) with shifting digits.
Transform digits into peg [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/peg.svg] labels: 0=A (#FFFFFF), 1=B (#87CEEB), 2=C (#90EE90).

sections.title: Mapping States to Ternary Coordinates
lecture_lines: Every disk configuration has a unique ternary address.
Higher digits represent larger disks in the stack.
For two disks, nine unique states cover all possibilities.
animations: Show a configuration: large disk on Peg A (0) and small disk on Peg C (2).
Write the ternary address '02' below the pegs, highlighting digits corresponding to disks.
Display a 3x3 grid of all 9 possible ternary states for two disks (00 to 22).

sections.title: The Geometry of Moves: The Sierpinski Gasket
lecture_lines: Valid moves connect states into a geometric graph.
One disk creates a simple three-node linear path.
Two disks form three connected lines in a triangle.
Three disks expand this structure into a larger triangle.
The resulting state graph forms a beautiful Sierpinski Gasket.
animations: Draw a 3-node horizontal graph (0-1-2) representing valid moves for one disk.
Replicate the line three times and connect the tips into a triangle for two disks.
Show the 9-vertex state graph where each edge is a valid disk move.
Assemble three 2-disk triangles into a larger triangle to represent three disks.
Highlight the final 27-vertex Sierpinski Gasket fractal representing the entire state space.

sections.title: Graph Traversal: Finding the Optimal Path
lecture_lines: Solving the puzzle means traversing the fractal's outer perimeter.
We travel from state 000 to state 222.
This golden path follows the constrained move rules.
Each step visits a new vertex along the edge.
The solution touches every node on the boundary.
animations: Focus on the 3-disk [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/disk.svg] Sierpinski Gasket and label the starting corner state 000.
Trace a glowing gold path (#FFD700) along the outer perimeter of the fractal.
Animate a moving point traveling from 000 through the middle and then to 222.
Flash each vertex on the perimeter as the path visits it in sequence.
Show that solving the puzzle [Asset: /mmfs1/data/home/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/puzzle.svg] requires visiting every node on the fractal boundary.

sections.title: Conclusion: The Beauty of Mathematical Convergence
lecture_lines: Ternary logic and fractals reveal the same underlying truth.
Simple recursive rules build infinite, self-similar geometric patterns.
Counting, graphs, and geometry converge in this restricted puzzle.
animations: Overlay ternary strings onto the vertices of the Sierpinski Gasket graph.
Zoom out the camera to reveal a higher-order Sierpinski Gasket (N=6).
